title: Casimir effect
description: Two metal plates a hair's breadth apart in a vacuum are pushed together by the restless energy of empty space. The force is tiny, but it makes the parts of micromachines stick.
effect: empty space pushes two very close plates together
pickWhy: Borderline: famous and real, but far too weak to do any job at a useful size. Drop unless you want effects for far-future candidates.
edbDesc: Physical forces arising from a quantized field. The typical example is of two uncharged metallic plates in a vacuum, placed a few micrometers apart, without any external electromagnetic field
